related_resources.reason: Sinusoidal response, superposition, harmonic forcing and resonance.
Fourier coefficients, orthogonality, period and harmonic decomposition.
Integrating factors, forcing terms, and examples.

authorship.scope: Original foundation-first Fourier and periodic-forcing lecture with non-spoken mathematical companion; earlier manuscripts retained.

prerequisites.reason: Solve first-order linear initial-value problems using integrating factors.
Resolve the switching input into its odd sine harmonics.
Distinguish Fourier convergence from justified termwise differentiation.

recommended.reason: Optional review of sinusoidal motion, period, amplitude and phase.

background: Elementary calculus, sine and cosine, first-order initial-value problems, and basic forced oscillators; no functional analysis or PDE background.
readiness_checks: Derive the response to sine forcing for y prime plus a times y equals f.
Match two exact solution pieces to find a unique periodic output.
Distinguish initial transients from periodic particular responses.

description: Solves first-order linear systems under periodic forcing, deriving the steady frequency response and separating transients from sustained oscillations.
